section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section summarizes findings from three studies on the development and psychometric evaluation of the BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2) with college and online community (MTurk) samples of women and men from the U.S. The BAS-2 demonstrated strong psychometric properties, measurement invariance across gender and sample type, and improved upon the original BAS by eliminating sex-specific versions and reflecting current positive body image understanding. Study 2 specifically found that college men reported higher body appreciation than college women (moderate difference), while community women and men showed minimal differences; additionally, the BAS-2 was inversely related to BMI to a moderate degree across all groups, with this relationship potentially reflecting cultural bias toward leanness in Western countries.
